title: a name as written is a married name only for a woman
line: the alias a decision writes from the name a record gives reads a married surname as the matcher does, a woman's only: Robert Edgar Davidson's obituary names Charles Miller, a son-in-law, and the owner accepts the card an older matcher left putting him to Charles Beckam Davidson; the son-in-law of that surname on the record is himself, and the record and the tree both say he is a man, so Charles Miller is no married name of his

steps.say: Robert Edgar Davidson's obituary, naming his brothers and sisters, his daughter Carol Miller and her husband Charles Miller
its subject accepted by the owner: the rule creates the brothers and sisters it names, Charles Beckam Davidson among them
a card an older matcher left, putting the son-in-law Charles Miller to Charles Beckam Davidson
the owner accepts that card all the same

expect.why: the record writes him Charles Miller beside a son-in-law of that surname, himself, but the record and the tree both say he is a man: his name as written is no married name, as the matcher reads none for him
